stem.en: Mesopotamian tablets name a place called Meluhha, and the book says it is "generally identified" with the Sindhu-Sarasvati civilisation. Which find would do the most to settle this?

text.en: A text naming Meluhha in both cuneiform and the Harappan script
More Harappan beads in Mesopotamian cities

feedback.en: Beads would show more trade. They would not show what the Harappans were called.

text.en: A longer list of goods from Meluhha in cuneiform

feedback.en: This adds to the Mesopotamian side only. It still does not link the name to a place on the ground.

text.en: A larger Harappan seal with more signs

feedback.en: More signs would help a little, but the script is still unread, so it could not tell us the name.

explanation.en: The word Meluhha comes only from the Mesopotamian side, and beads and the sea route make the match likely. A text naming Meluhha in both scripts would link the name to the Harappans, and it could also help to read the Harappan script.

hints.en: Which find would join the writing of both sides?
